body.p: This listing of claims will replace all prior versions, and listings, of claims in the application:

br.br:
Claim 1 (currently amended): A method of controlling a rotor assembly of a tiltrotor aircraft comprising:automatically changing a rotor speed of the rotor assembly of the tiltrotor aircraft while moving the rotor assembly or a pylon thereof from a first rotor position and a first rotor speed to a second rotor position and a second rotor speed over a time period in accordance with an acceleration-rate profile that varies over the time period using a controller communicably coupled to the rotor assembly of the tiltrotor aircraft.
Claim 2 (currently amended): The method of claim 1, further comprising receiving a signal at the controller to change the rotor assembly or the pylon thereof from the first rotor position to the second rotor position.
Claim 3 (currently amended): The method of claim 1, wherein:the first rotor position of the rotor assembly or the pylon thereof corresponds to a takeoff- and-landing mode or a hover mode, and the second rotor position of the rotor assembly or the pylon thereof corresponds to a cruise mode; or the first rotor position of the rotor assembly or the pylon thereof corresponds the cruise mode, and the second rotor position of the rotor assembly or the pylon thereof corresponds to the takeoff-and-landing mode or the hover mode.
Claim 4 (currently amended): The method of claim 1, wherein:the first rotor position of the rotor assembly or the pylon thereof is generally parallel to a yaw axis of the tiltrotor aircraft, and the second rotor position of the rotor assembly or pylon thereof is generally parallel to a roll axis of the tiltrotor aircraft; or the first rotor position of the rotor assembly or the pylon thereof is generally parallel to the roll axis of the tiltrotor aircraft, and the second rotor position of the rotor assembly or the pylon thereof is generally parallel to the yaw axis of the tiltrotor aircraft.
Claim 5 (previously presented): The method of claim 1, further comprising determining the acceleration-rate profile based on one or more operational parameters comprising one or more of a rotor assembly performance parameter, an aircraft operational mode parameter, an aircraft characteristic parameter, or an environmental parameter.
Claim 6 (original): The method of claim 5, further comprising determining the one or more operational parameters based on one or more sensors communicably coupled to the controller, one or more flight controls communicably coupled to the controller, or one or more signals from one or more remote devices communicably coupled to the controller.
Claim 7 (original): The method of claim 1, wherein the acceleration-rate profile comprises a multi- segment linear profile, a curved profile, a stair-stepped profile, or a combination thereof.
Claim 8 (original): The method of claim 1, wherein the acceleration-rate profile comprises at least one curved segment and at least one linear segment.
Claim 9 (original): The method of claim 1, wherein the acceleration-rate profile comprises an increasing acceleration rate for a first portion of the time period, a constant acceleration rate for a second portion of the time period, and a decreasing acceleration rate for a third portion of the time period.
Claim 10 (original): The method of claim 1, wherein the rotor speed is changed over the time period according to a portion of the time period remaining in the time period or a difference between an actual rotor speed and a reference rotor speed.
Claim 11 (original): The method of claim 1, wherein the acceleration-rate profile is implemented using to a control law based on a reference rotor speed and an actual rotor speed.
Claim 12 (original): The method of claim 11, wherein the control law comprises a variable acceleration command based on a portion of the time period remaining in the time period or a difference between the actual rotor speed and the reference rotor speed.
Claim 13 (original): The method of claim 1, wherein the controller is an analog device, a digital device, or a combination thereof.
Claim 14 (original): The method of claim 1, wherein the rotor speed is changed using the controller and at least one of a collective governor or a throttle governor.
Claim 15 (original): The method of claim 1, wherein the rotor speed is changed by changing a reference rotor speed.
Claim 16 (currently amended): An apparatus for controlling a rotor assembly system of a tiltrotor aircraft, comprising:a controller operably coupled to the rotor assembly and operably configured to automatically change a rotor speed of the rotor assembly of the tiltrotor aircraft while moving the rotor assembly or the pylon thereof from a first rotor position and a first rotor speed to a second rotor position and a second rotor speed over a time period in accordance with an acceleration-rate profile that varies over the time period.
Claim 17 (previously presented): The apparatus of claim 16, further comprising one or more control devices or one or more remote devices communicably coupled to the controller that
operably configured to send or receive a signal to change the rotor assembly or the pylon thereof from the first rotor speed to the second rotor speed.
Claim 18 (original): The apparatus of claim 17, wherein the one or more control devices comprise a collective governor or a throttle governor.
